clue.text: "Former champion has confused an artist with a river, Virginia".

indicators.note: confused tells us the three letters of the word has are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
VA is the US postal abbreviation for the state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A muddled report that a past winner has gone off with a painter to a river in Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns HAS into SHA. Maria Sharapova won Wimbledon in 2004, the first of the tennis names in this themed grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Sharapova is a Russian tennis player who won all four Grand Slam titles, now retired.

clue.text: Spin a share

definitions.meaning: in tennis or golf a ... is a cut stroke that puts sideways spin on the ball
a ... of the cake or profits is a portion or cut

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a slicing stroke that spins the ball, and a portion cut from a whole.

clue.text: Get garage to put together total

indicators.note: putting the letters together afresh tells us to rebuild these two words into a single new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions to get the garage to add up the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put together' rearranges the nine letters of GET GARAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aggregate is a sum formed by adding parts together, a synonym for a total.

clue.text: Achieve something at tennis, first with one in Scotland

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word tennis that it follows

parts.note: ain is a Scots form of the word one, as in the Scots speech of the Lowlands

explanation.surface: Someone scores a success at tennis, coming first alongside a competitor in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes only T from 'tennis'; 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain is to reach or gain a goal, which is to achieve something.

clue.text: Charade to produce things with many faces

indicators.note: produce asks the letters of charade and to to be worked into a fresh word, as raw material makes goods

explanation.surface: A game of charades is being used to stage something two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produce' rearranges the nine letters of CHARADE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Octahedra are solid figures each bounded by eight plane faces, so plural shapes with many faces.

clue.text: Declare it's pretty ordinary with age

indicators.note: the clue says the answer with age added is the ordinary word, so taking that word away from it leaves the answer

parts.note: average means pretty ordinary, nothing special
taken as written as a synonym of itself: the letters of age

explanation.surface: Someone states that things become fairly humdrum as the years pass.
explanation.walkthrough: This is read in reverse: put 'age' after the answer and you have the word for pretty ordinary, so 'with' names the piece that has to come off.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert, so it means to declare.

clue.text: It passes through a prism, a shaft of light overhead

indicators.note: the answer is a run of letters passing through the words, sitting across the gaps between them

explanation.surface: A description of light passing through a glass prism, with a beam shining from above.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'priSM A SHaft'. 'Overhead' is the tennis definition, not part of the optics picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a smash is a hard downward stroke hit from above the head, an overhead shot.

clue.text: As to aces, they may become marginal

definitions.note: used loosely as a noun: land at the margin of the sea

indicators.note: may become tells us these letters can turn into something else when reordered

explanation.surface: Aces in a tennis serve are said to be in danger of becoming borderline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may become' rearranges the eight letters of AS TO ACES; 'they' links the fodder to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A seacoast is the land along the sea's edge, the margin of a country.

clue.text: Put on to protect the stage perhaps

definitions.meaning: a garment worn over clothes to keep them clean while cooking
the part of a theatre stage projecting in front of the curtain, or an airport's hardstanding

explanation.definitionFit: An apron is both a protective garment tied over clothes and the forward part of a stage.

clue.text: Changing shoes sets them up as entertainers

indicators.note: changing tells us the order of the letters in these two words is altered

explanation.surface: Someone trying on footwear sets them up as performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing' rearranges the nine letters of SHOES SETS; 'them up as' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostesses receive and entertain guests at a party, so they are people who entertain.

clue.text: Block obtained after I took direction

indicators.note: after places the word for obtained behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: N for north, one of the compass points
got is a past tense of get, meaning obtained

explanation.surface: Someone receives a block after following instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'took' only joins the I to the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a block of cast metal, such as gold or silver.

clue.text: He's coming in to sign a dictionary

indicators.note: coming in to tells us one piece enters another and sits inside it

parts.note: Taurus, the bull, is a sign of the zodiac
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man joins an astrological sign to produce a reference book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in to' reads as 'coming into': the pronoun with its apostrophe is placed inside the star sign after its opening T.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms, a kind of dictionary of words grouped by meaning.

clue.text: Peers mostly right about the quality of viewing

parts.note: to peer at something is to look hard, so peers means eyes as a verb

indicators.note: mostly says most of the word right is kept, here all but its opening letter

explanation.surface: A remark that members of the House of Lords are largely correct about how good television is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' looks like the Lords, but it is the verb for looking. 'mostly' usually drops a last letter; here RIGHT loses its first to give IGHT. 'about' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty or power of seeing, how well a person sees.

clue.text: Showing self-confidence that is largely lightweight

annotationWithheld.why: Showing self-confidence that is largely lightweight (6): B + OUNCE (lightweight) is likely, but no clue word fairly supplies the B and the definition/wordplay split could not be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Showing self-confidence that is largely lightweight

clue.text: A note to the police about an imperfection

parts.note: F is a musical note of the scale
the law is a slang name for the police

explanation.surface: Writing a letter to the police complaining about a defect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'about' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: A flaw is a defect or blemish, so it is an imperfection.

clue.text: Penalty for overstepping the mark

parts.note: in tennis a server who steps on or over the baseline while serving is penalised

explanation.definitionFit: A tennis fault called when a server's foot crosses the baseline, literally overstepping a marked line.

clue.text: Short teasers designed to make a point at court

definitions.text: Short teasers designed to make a point at court

parts.words: Short teasers designed to make a point at court
parts.note: a soft tennis stroke that barely clears the net teases the opponent and wins a point

explanation.definitionFit: Gentle shots that fall just over the net, short of the opponent, to win points on court.

clue.text: Agape, like Belloc's Ponto was

definitions.meaning: with the mouth wide open in wonder
Ponto is the lion in Hilaire Belloc's cautionary tale of Jim, who was eaten after running from his nurse

explanation.definitionFit: Open-jawed means gaping, mouth wide, which suits both an amazed onlooker and a lion about to bite.

clue.text: Unaware of what's clear about one pound

indicators.note: about tells us the word for clear wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: something obvious is plain and clear
one pound is £1, written L1 with L for libra, and the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone fails to notice a pound coin lying in plain view.
explanation.walkthrough: One pound, £1, is written L1, and the figure is taken as the letter I; 'of' just links the definition to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being oblivious means having no awareness of what is going on around one.

clue.text: Mysterious about rice following return to the south-east

indicators.note: following places the rearranged rice after the turned-round pieces
return tells us the word to and the compass abbreviation are read backwards together

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: about here means in a rough or turned-around order, so the letters of rice are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzling story of rice served after a trip back to the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns TO SE into ESOT; 'about' rearranges RICE into ERIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by an inner circle, hence obscure or mysterious.

clue.text: Exaggerate deliveries to the country

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Someone overplays the importance of shipments to a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a cricket term: a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstate is to make something sound greater than it is, to exaggerate.

clue.text: Donations for weapons by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it tells us the word is judged by how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: arms are weapons

explanation.surface: Gifts of weaponry, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: In British non-rhotic speech the R of ARMS is silent, so it is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts of money or food given to the poor, charitable donations.

clue.text: Short account of first sailing vessel

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word sailing

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A brief history of the earliest sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a brief outline or description, a short account of something.

clue.text: Loyalty may be late in following year

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the two abbreviations

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: may be signals that the letters of late can be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A remark that faithfulness may wane later in the following year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges LATE into EALT. F and Y are the usual abbreviations for following and year; the blogger read them as FY, following year.
explanation.definitionFit: Fealty is the loyalty a vassal owed a feudal lord, sworn allegiance.

clue.text: An extra returns with a show of assent the first two days

indicators.note: returns tells us the word for assent and the picked letters are read backwards together

parts.note: a nod of the head signals agreement

indicators.note: the first two takes just the opening pair of letters of the word days

explanation.surface: A bonus comes back with someone nodding approval for the first couple of days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first two' takes DA from 'days'; 'returns' turns NOD DA into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An add-on is something attached as a supplement, an extra.

clue.text: "One of the favourites started in formal attire alright but has nothing on, Victoria!"

indicators.note: on puts the round letter in front of the short name, as if resting upon it

parts.note: DJ is short for dinner jacket, formal evening wear
OK means alright
O looks like zero, nothing
Vic is a short form of the name Victoria

explanation.surface: A gossip column claims a favourite began in a tuxedo but is now naked, shocking a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started in' and 'but has' only link the pieces. Novak Djokovic is the Serbian tennis champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Novak Djokovic, winner of many Grand Slam titles, was one of the tennis favourites to win.

clue.text: Civil engineer holds one material and creates another

indicators.note: holds tells us the abbreviation contains the fabric within it

parts.note: rep is a corded fabric used for upholstery

explanation.surface: An engineer keeps one fabric and makes a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the definition: it stands for another material, picking up 'material' earlier in the clue, and 'and creates' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepe is a thin crinkled fabric, a further material besides the first one named.

clue.text: Criticise a version of 19

indicators.note: a version of tells us the letters of the earlier answer appear in a different form

parts.note: 19-across, whose answer is the word for charitable gifts

explanation.surface: An instruction to knock another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the letters of 19-across gives the answer, which also nods to the tennis theme: a Grand Slam.
explanation.definitionFit: To slam something is to criticise it harshly, as a reviewer might a play.

clue.text: A wonderful way with deep water

indicators.note: a way of arranging the letters of wonderful tells us they are reordered

explanation.surface: Praise for a marvellous route through the deep sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' rearranges the nine letters of WONDERFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An underflow is a current running below the surface, water flowing at depth.

clue.text: The first cord, figuratively speaking

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase defining the noun for a figure of speech

indicators.note: first picks only the opening letter of the word The

parts.note: a rope is a thick cord

explanation.surface: A remark about the original string, meant metaphorically.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech, a word used figuratively rather than literally.

clue.text: Military uniform is cut in a different way

indicators.note: a different way tells us these letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: A soldier's jacket is tailored differently.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is 'a different way', which rearranges CUT IN, so 'in' belongs to the fodder; 'is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket worn as part of a soldier's or police uniform.

clue.text: A crazy start by England has the heartless rushed

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: start takes the opening letter of the word England

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A wild beginning by England's side rushed off without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the H from THE to leave TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Made haste is an idiom meaning hurried, past tense of make haste.
